div: The LLM Assistant lets you work with InterSpec by typing questions and instructions in plain language. A large-language-model (LLM) reads your request together with context about the currently displayed spectrum, and then drives InterSpec's own tools on your behalf — fitting peaks, identifying nuclides, calculating decays, adjusting energy calibration, running activity/shielding and isotopic analyses, and explaining what it finds.

The assistant is opened as a tab (or window) titled "LLM Assistant". The large area shows the conversation, and you type into the input field at the bottom. Results, tool calls, and the assistant's reasoning appear in the conversation as you go.

While the assistant is working, the send button becomes a stop button. If you stop it, or a request to the LLM fails, an error appears where the work stopped. For the assistant itself, "Retry" sends the request again, and "Skip" drops it so you can ask something else. For one of its specialized agents (for example the nuclide-identification agent), "Retry" continues the agent from where it stopped, and "Cancel Agent" lets the assistant carry on without it; asking a new question instead also leaves it behind.

You can instead show the assistant in a full-height panel to the right of the spectrum, using "Show to Right of Spectrum" in its menu (on phones held in landscape, use the shrink button at the top of the full-screen assistant); drag the panel's left edge to change its width. The button at the top of the panel moves the assistant back. InterSpec remembers where you last had the assistant, and the panel's width, for the next time you open it.

div.p: Before you can chat, the assistant needs an LLM provider, a model, and (for most providers) an API key. If nothing is configured yet, the tool shows a "Configure LLM Provider" button; you can also open the settings at any time from the tool's menu ("Configure LLM Provider…") - see Conversation Menu below.

In the settings window you choose the provider (for example a hosted API endpoint or a locally running model) - a drop-down next to the endpoint fills in the endpoint for well-known providers - enter the bearer token/key, and pick the model name to use. For models InterSpec knows about, the model's settings are filled in for you. Configuration is validated, and warnings are shown if, for example, the endpoint or key looks unset. Your settings are saved so you do not have to re-enter them each session.
See the "Configuring an LLM Provider" help topic (under this topic, or via the help icon in the settings window) for what to enter for each provider, and what each setting does.

Type a question or instruction and press Enter (or the Send button). You can refer to the spectrum you have loaded and to peaks you have already fit — the assistant is given that context automatically. Some examples of what you can ask:

ul.li: "What nuclides could be producing the peaks in this spectrum?"
"Fit the peak near 662 keV and tell me its net area."
"Is the 1460 keV peak consistent with K-40 background?"
"Check the energy calibration against the Th-232 and K-40 lines."
"Estimate the U-235 enrichment from these peaks."
"What is the activity of Cs-137, assuming 5 cm of steel shielding?"

div.p: The assistant works best when the peaks of interest have been fit — it can fit peaks for you, but you can often get better results on difficult regions by fitting them yourself first. It may take several tool calls to answer a single question; you will see each step appear in the conversation.

If the configured model supports vision, you can send an image along with your message — for example a photograph of an instrument display, a screenshot of another program, or a plot you want the assistant to interpret. There are two ways to attach an image:

ul.li: Drag‑and‑drop a file onto InterSpec: drop an image file (PNG, JPEG, etc.) anywhere on the app window. InterSpec shows the image, along with a "Send to LLM assistant" button; click it to attach the image to your next message. A thumbnail of the attached image appears just above the input field.

Paste into the input field: copy an image to your clipboard (for example with a screenshot tool) and paste it directly into the message input area with Ctrl‑V (Cmd‑V on macOS). A thumbnail appears above the input field. Pasting text works as normal — only image clipboard content is captured as an attachment.

div.p: You can type a message describing what you want (for example "What isotope does this instrument readout suggest?") together with the attached image, then press Enter or the Send button. To remove a staged image before sending, click the small remove control on its thumbnail.

Image size limits. To keep requests small, images are resized in your browser before being sent to the provider. An image larger than 2048 pixels on its longest side is scaled down so its longest side is 2048 pixels, preserving the aspect ratio; smaller images are sent at their original size. PNG images are kept as PNG; other formats are re‑encoded as JPEG (at about 85% quality). Because of this resizing and re‑encoding, very fine detail or text in a large image may be reduced — crop to the region of interest first if the details matter.

The menu icon (⋯) at the left of the input box - or in the title bar, when the assistant is shown to the right of the spectrum, and at the top right of the full-screen assistant on phones - provides conversation-level actions (the last four are not available on phones):

table.style: text-align: left; border: 1px solid black; border-collapse: collapse;

tr.td: Discard the current conversation and start fresh.
Summarize older parts of the conversation to reduce how much context is sent to the model, while keeping the important results. Useful for long sessions.
Move the assistant into a full-height panel to the right of the spectrum. The button in the panel's title bar moves it back.

Show the details useful when developing the assistant: each tool call's parameters in full and its raw result, menus on each panel to view the JSON sent to and from the LLM (and to ask a sub-agent a follow-up question), and the two menu items below. Remembered for next time.
(With debug options shown.) Save the full conversation (your messages, the assistant's replies, and the tool calls it made) to a JSON file.
(With debug options shown.) Re-read the configuration from disk and start a new session with it.

div.p: When you send a message, your prompt is sent — along with context describing the displayed spectrum and its fit peaks — to the LLM provider you configured. Anything the assistant needs to answer (peak energies, areas, nuclide candidates, and similar analysis data) may be transmitted to that provider. Do not use a provider or model that is not approved for the sensitivity of the data you are analyzing. If you need everything to stay local, configure a locally hosted model rather than a remote hosted API.
The assistant is a tool to accelerate analysis, not a substitute for expert judgment. Always review its suggested identifications and quantitative results before relying on them.
